cases.description: a dry run names what registering would refuse and what it would change, and applies nothing: the registered document stays as it was
registering and its dry run are the schema grant's: write, read and no token are refused, before anything of the document is answered
a registration naming a revision the record store no longer holds is a conflict and applies nothing; naming the current one applies it
a document that is the registered one rewritten byte for byte differently is unchanged: no new revision, the registered text stays as it was, and writes still apply

a document that adds a record type to the registered module is a compatible change: a dry run says so and applies nothing, registering it makes a new revision that readers see, and registering it again changes nothing
a replica is fed, never registered: it has no dry run either, and says so
an export is every entity by type then key, then every relationship; a property that is not set, and an author or time the record never had, are absent, never null
a person with no read on the module, or no token, is Refused, never given an empty page; a backend that is down is Unavailable
a page resumes after the last record it gave, so a write between pages neither repeats nor skips a record, and the pages together are the whole export
a replica holds a copy, not the authoritative records, and says so rather than export them
